newsitem.title: USA: Court upholds contempt citation against McDougal.
newsitem.headline: Court upholds contempt citation against McDougal.

text.p: A federal court upheld on Wednesday a contempt citation that put Susan McDougal in jail last month for refusing to testify about President Bill Clinton's role in the Whitewater saga.

A three-judge panel of the Eighth Circuit Court of Appeals rejected a complaint by McDougal, a former business partner of Clinton and Hillary Rodham Clinton, that her constitutional rights were violated when a district judge found her in contempt of court and sent her to jail one month ago.

McDougal refused to testify before a grand jury, saying prosecutors investigating the Whitewater affair were pressing her to invent evidence implicating the president and first lady in illegal business deals. But the appeals court rejected her claim that she deserved a hearing on the reasons for her refusal to testify.

"The defendant has not been irretrievably deprived of her liberty; she may end her incarceration at any time simply by agreeing to testify," the judges said. The ruling means McDougal could serve up to 17 months more for contempt of court unless she agrees to cooperate with the team of independent counsel Kenneth Starr and talk to the grand jury.
In a series of recent interviews from a detention centre in Conway, Ark., McDougal has said she will not back down.
She was found guilty on four counts of fraud in the first Whitewater trial this year and was sentenced to two years in prison. She has yet to begin serving that sentence.

Clinton was not accused of any crime in the trial but was called to testify to answer allegations he twice pressured an Arkansas banker to give Susan McDougal an illegal $300,000 loan in 1986, when he was governor of Arkansas.

Proceeds from the loan allegedly went to pay some expenses of the ill-fated Whitewater real estate venture in northern Arkansas in which McDougal and her ex-husband James McDougal were partners of the Clintons.

James McDougal was convicted on a string of fraud and conspiracy charges and faces up to 84 years in prison but sentencing was postponed until November because he agreed to cooperate with Starr's team. It is not known what information he has provided.
